To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dielectric properties of the myocardium change significantly during myocardial ischemia and infarction, that these changes are detectable in vivo by microwave spectroscopy, and that the changes can be used to monitor the development and extent of ischemia and infarcation.
the proposed dielectrical model of myocardium can be used to reconstruct tissue properties of myocardium in vivo.

the proposed model of dielectric relaxation of the myocardium is verified by both experimental data on test solutions and normal myocardium and can be utilized for reconstruction of the tissue properties (myocardial resistance and water concentration) in acute myocardial ischemia and in chronic myocardial infarction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of microwave spectroscopy for the study of myocardial ischemia and infarction.
the study of the dielectric properties of the myocardium, and the development of an analytical model of myocardial dielectric properties.
the development of a noninvasive microwave spectroscopic technique for monitoring of the myocardium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed dielectric relaxation model for myocardial tissue is valid and that it may serve as a basis for a quantitative reconstruction of the myocardium properties following acute myocardial ischemia or infarction.
microwave spectroscopy is a powerful tool for noninvasive monitoring of acute myocardial infarction and for detection of the chronic myocardial scar.
the proposed dielectric relaxation model of the normal myocardium in the 0-3 GHz microwave spectrum has been experimentally verified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed dielectrical model of the myocardial tissue can be used for biophysical reconstruction of myocardial ischemia and infarction.

the proposed model is capable of reconstructing the tissue properties in the microwave spectrum, and that this model can be used as a tool to monitor the development and evolution of acute and chronic myocardial ischemia and infarction.
we have shown that microwave spectroscopy is a very sensitive technique to detect changes in the myocardium following acute ischemia and in chronic infarcted tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed dielectrical model of the myocardial tissue is capable of reconstructing changes in myocardial properties during the acute and chronic phases of ischemia and infarction.
microwave spectroscopy can be used to monitor the process of acute myocardial tissue injury and to detect chronic myocardial infarction.
the proposed dielectric relaxation model can be used to characterize the changes of myocardial tissue properties following ischemia and infarction.
